rule.rule_name: Akamai API Security: disbursal endpoint velocity or dummy reference value
rule.summary: Uses Akamai API Security findings to flag a source IP that hits payment or disbursal endpoints more than 15 times in 5 minutes, or that sends a reference-type parameter with a placeholder value such as 000000, 123456, test or dummy.
rule.query:
config case_sensitive = false
| dataset = akamai_api_security_raw
| alter finding_type = json_extract_scalar(to_json_string(event), "$.typeName"),
        finding_desc = json_extract_scalar(to_json_string(event), "$.description"),
        evidence = json_extract_array(to_json_string(event), "$.evidence")
| arrayexpand evidence
| alter req_host = json_extract_scalar(evidence, "$.host"),
        req_path = json_extract_scalar(evidence, "$.path"),
        req_method = json_extract_scalar(evidence, "$.method"),
        req_status = json_extract_scalar(evidence, "$.statusCode"),
        req_src_ip = json_extract_scalar(evidence, "$.sourceIp")
| filter req_path ~= "(?i)/(disburs|payout|payment|refund|transfer|settle)"
| alter param_field = arrayindex(regextract(finding_desc, "Field:\\s*([^\\n]+)"), 0),
        param_value = arrayindex(regextract(finding_desc, "Value:\\s*([^\\n]+)"), 0)
| alter is_dummy_ref = if(param_field ~= "(?i)(ref|utr|txn|transaction|reference)" and param_value ~= "(?i)^\\s*(0+|1+|9+|1234[0-9]*|test.*|dummy.*|x{3,}|na|null|none)\\s*$", 1, 0)
| bin _time span = 5m
| comp count() as call_count, sum(is_dummy_ref) as dummy_ref_count, values(req_path) as paths, values(req_host) as hosts, values(finding_type) as finding_types by _time, req_src_ip
| filter call_count > 15 or dummy_ref_count > 0
| alter trigger_reason = if(dummy_ref_count > 0 and call_count > 15, "velocity + dummy reference", if(dummy_ref_count > 0, "dummy reference value", "velocity > 15 calls / 5 min"))
| fields _time, req_src_ip, call_count, dummy_ref_count, trigger_reason, paths, hosts, finding_types
| sort desc call_count
logic_explanation: Reads Akamai API Security findings from akamai_api_security_raw. Each event is a finding whose nested 'event' object holds the finding type, a description, and an 'evidence' array of the requests that triggered it.
Extracts the evidence array with json_extract_array and expands it with arrayexpand, so each evidence request (host, path, method, status, source IP) becomes its own row.
Keeps only requests to payment or disbursal paths (/disburs, /payout, /payment, /refund, /transfer, /settle).

Pulls the parameter name and value out of the finding description ('Field: ... Value: ...') with regextract, and marks the row as a dummy reference when a reference-type field (ref, utr, txn, transaction, reference) carries a placeholder value.
Buckets rows into 5-minute windows and counts requests and dummy-reference hits per source IP.
Fires when a source IP has more than 15 disbursal requests in a window or any dummy reference value, and labels which condition triggered.
assumptions: Important: akamai_api_security_raw holds API Security findings, not every API request. The evidence array only lists the requests attached to each finding, so call_count is a lower bound and true '15 calls in 5 minutes' velocity can be missed. For exact velocity, run the same logic on Akamai's full traffic logs (for example the Akamai WAF / SIEM or DataStream dataset) if you ingest them.
Assumes the nested 'event' column is stored as JSON. to_json_string is used so the query works whether XSIAM stored it as an object or a string.
Bucketing uses the finding's _time, not the evidence requestTs. If findings are reported with a delay, switch to the parsed evidence timestamp.
Dummy values are detected only when Akamai reports them in the finding description (as in parameter-out-of-range findings). Values that Akamai does not flag are not visible in this dataset.
The disbursal path keywords and reference field names are guesses. Replace them with the application's real routes and parameter names.
false_positives: Mobile clients behind carrier-grade NAT (many users on one IPv6/IPv4 address) can inflate per-IP counts.
Out-of-range findings where a value of 0 or 1 is legitimate for that field.
Internal testing or QA traffic against production APIs.
tuning: Restrict to the relevant hosts with: filter req_host in ("<your API host>").
Exclude known partner and internal IP ranges with incidr() or a lookup dataset.
Raise the threshold or filter on finding_type if particular Akamai finding types are noisy.
Add organisation-specific dummy values (for example REF0000) to the regex.
rule.testing: First run the query without the final 'filter call_count > 15 or dummy_ref_count > 0' over the last 24 hours to confirm that the evidence fields extract correctly (non-empty req_path and req_src_ip). Then lower the threshold temporarily (for example call_count > 1) to see sample hits. To deploy, save it as a correlation rule that runs every 5 minutes over a 5-minute time frame, with suppression on req_src_ip.

variants.name: Field check: confirm the evidence fields parse (run first, last 24 hours)

dataset = akamai_api_security_raw
| alter evidence = json_extract_array(to_json_string(event), "$.evidence")
| arrayexpand evidence
| alter req_path = json_extract_scalar(evidence, "$.path"), req_src_ip = json_extract_scalar(evidence, "$.sourceIp"), finding_type = json_extract_scalar(to_json_string(event), "$.typeName")
| fields _time, finding_type, req_path, req_src_ip
| limit 50

title: Disbursal API Velocity & Bypassed Workflow Rule

request.requirement: Logic: Monitors payment/disbursal endpoints for >15 invocations in 5 minutes or requests carrying dummy reference numbers.
request.logic: Logic: Monitors payment/disbursal endpoints for >15 invocations in 5 minutes or requests carrying dummy reference numbers.

rule.rule_name: Disbursal API velocity or dummy reference number
rule.summary: Flags a source IP or user that calls payment or disbursal API endpoints more than 15 times in 5 minutes, or sends a disbursal request with a placeholder reference number (all zeros, 123456, test, dummy, xxxx, null). Both patterns point to scripted abuse, testing in production, or someone pushing payouts outside the normal approval workflow.
rule.query:
config case_sensitive = false
| datamodel dataset = your_api_gateway_raw
| filter xdm.network.http.url ~= "(?i)/(disburs|payout|payment|transfer)"
| alter is_dummy_ref = if(xdm.network.http.url ~= "(?i)[?&](ref|ref_no|refno|reference|reference_no|utr|txn_ref|txnref|transaction_ref)=(0+|1+|9+|1234[0-9]*|test[^&]*|dummy[^&]*|x{3,}|na|null|none)(&|$)", 1, 0)
| bin _time span = 5m
| comp count() as call_count, sum(is_dummy_ref) as dummy_ref_count, values(xdm.network.http.url) as sample_urls by _time, xdm.source.ipv4, xdm.source.user.username
| filter call_count > 15 or dummy_ref_count > 0
| alter trigger_reason = if(dummy_ref_count > 0 and call_count > 15, "velocity + dummy reference", if(dummy_ref_count > 0, "dummy reference number", "velocity > 15 calls / 5 min"))
| fields _time, xdm.source.ipv4, xdm.source.user.username, call_count, dummy_ref_count, trigger_reason, sample_urls
| sort desc call_count
logic_explanation: Queries the Cortex Data Model (XDM) so the rule works with any API gateway, WAF or load-balancer log source that is mapped to XDM. Replace your_api_gateway_raw with your dataset name.
Keeps only requests whose URL contains a payment or disbursal path (/disburs, /payout, /payment, /transfer).

Marks a request as is_dummy_ref = 1 when a reference parameter (ref, reference, utr, txn_ref, ...) holds a placeholder value such as 000000, 111111, 999999, 123456..., test, dummy, xxxx, na, null or none.
Buckets events into 5-minute windows with bin, then counts calls and dummy-reference hits per source IP and user in each window.
Fires when a source makes more than 15 calls in a window, or sends at least one dummy reference, and labels which condition triggered it.
assumptions: Data source was not specified. The query assumes your API gateway / WAF logs are ingested and mapped to XDM. Replace your_api_gateway_raw with the real dataset (for example an F5, Kong, Apigee, AWS API Gateway or NGINX *_raw dataset).

Assumes the full request URL, including the query string, is mapped to xdm.network.http.url. If the reference number is sent in the JSON body instead, point the is_dummy_ref regex at the raw body field (for example your_api_gateway_raw.request_body).
Endpoint paths (/disburs, /payout, /payment, /transfer) and the reference parameter names are guesses. Replace them with your application's real routes and parameter names.

The title mentions a bypassed workflow. This version detects it through dummy reference numbers only. A rule that confirms the approval step was skipped (disbursal with no prior /approve call in the same session) needs a join against the approval endpoint. Comment /regenerate with your approval route if you want that version.
XQL regex uses RE2, so repeated-digit patterns such as 222222 are not matched generically. Only the listed placeholders are caught.
false_positives: Legitimate batch jobs or reconciliation services that call disbursal APIs in bursts.
QA or UAT traffic that uses test reference numbers against the production gateway.
Health checks or monitoring probes that hit payment endpoints.
Several users behind one NAT or proxy IP, which inflates per-IP counts when the username is empty.
tuning: Exclude known batch and service accounts and internal scanner IPs with: filter xdm.source.user.username not in ("svc_batch", ...).
Baseline normal peak volume per client for a week, then raise the threshold above 15 if needed.
Group by an API key or client ID field instead of IP if your logs carry one. It is more accurate behind NAT.
Add your organisation's own known dummy values (for example REF0000) to the regex.
rule.testing: In a test window, send 16 or more requests to a disbursal endpoint from one test client within 5 minutes, and a single request with ?ref=000000. Run the query over the last hour and confirm both rows appear with the right trigger_reason. To deploy, save it as a correlation rule that runs every 5 minutes over a 5-minute query time frame, with issue suppression on xdm.source.ipv4 and xdm.source.user.username.

variants.name: Hunting: top disbursal callers, last 24 hours (run with time frame = 24 hours)
variants.query:
datamodel dataset = your_api_gateway_raw
| filter xdm.network.http.url ~= "(?i)/(disburs|payout|payment|transfer)"
| bin _time span = 5m
| comp count() as call_count by _time, xdm.source.ipv4, xdm.source.user.username
| comp max(call_count) as peak_5min, sum(call_count) as total_calls by xdm.source.ipv4, xdm.source.user.username
| sort desc peak_5min
| limit 50
